Part of the problem with Uma Nada-Rajah’s new play is that it can’t quite choose between the symbolism and the naturalism.
' Black Hole Sign’ , written by Uma Nada-Rajah portrays a fast-paced account of one night inside an understaffed NHS ward.
Black Hole Sign is an intelligently complex play that bears often funny, incisive witness to both the remarkable work of NHS staff and the precarious condition of Britain’s most beloved institution.
Black Hole Sign at the Tron Theatre is a sharp, funny, and through provoking new play that captures the chaos and humanity of an overstretched NHS ward.

cn.t: Critics praise this sharp, authentic NHS drama from nurse-playwright Uma Nada-Rajah for its hard-hitting realism and dark humor. The production effectively captures the chaos of an overstretched hospital ward through compelling characters and vivid storytelling.
